correctness.rationale: The chosen one-parameter subgroup preserves nilpotency and commutation. Powers of Q give pairwise distinct ordered off-diagonal conjugation weights, and a sufficiently large relative shift separates the two matrix factors. The only positive-dimensional ambient weight spaces are the diagonal subspaces, which contain no nonzero nilpotent matrices. Every off-diagonal matrix unit squares to zero, so the projective fixed locus on the commuting-nilpotent pair variety consists of exactly two copies of the n(n-1) off-diagonal coordinate points. Euler localization for algebraic C* actions then gives the stated value without a smoothness hypothesis.

value.rationale: The commuting-nilpotent pair variety is a classical singular variety linked to punctual Hilbert schemes, and its projective degree is already nontrivial enough to require substantial enumerative calculations. The theorem shows that ordinary Euler characteristic behaves in the opposite extreme: it is exactly the elementary quadratic count 2n(n-1) for every n. The contrast with the published degrees 4, 72, and 5440 for n=2,3,4 provides a sharp structural explanation of how coarse Euler characteristic is on this important family, while the fixed-point description is uniform and reusable.
